appraisal_events.evidence: The fidèles overcome their initial unease and formally welcome Charlus into their compartment ('nous nous acheminâmes tous vers le compartiment de M. de Charlus'); his mysterious 'vice' comes to make his conversation seem more intelligent than the others' ('on le trouvait plus intelligent que les autres'); and he becomes 'le fidèle des fidèles, une seconde princesse Sherbatoff' for Mme Verdurin, standing in for her hosting duties and greeting new arrivals at the station.
appraisal_events.explanation: Across the passage Charlus rises from a wary, half-excluded curiosity -- privately pitied by Cottard as friendless -- to the most trusted, most included figure in the little clan, though the fidèles' fascination is tinged with an exoticizing, almost freak-show curiosity about his hidden nature ('boîte de provenance exotique et suspecte').

appraisal_events.evidence: 'Des hommes brillants... à la Raspelière faisaient des avances et d'ennuyeux devenaient exquis. Ce fut le cas pour le prince de Guermantes,' who climbs to the Verdurins' door on his own initiative, driven by Dreyfusist enthusiasm, even without his wife present.
appraisal_events.explanation: The prince crosses from the category of men the Verdurins found boring and kept at a distance to a welcomed, even sought-after guest at the Raspelière.

appraisal_events.evidence: 'C'est peut-être un imbécile du Jockey,' Mme Verdurin says of the prince even as she schemes to put him on display, directing Charlus to stage a little fête in his honor.
appraisal_events.explanation: Even while promoting him for prestige, Mme Verdurin privately disparages the prince's intelligence, undercutting the elevation of E2 with casual contempt.

status_effects.explanation: The fidèles come to rate his conversation and intelligence above the others', even though they misattribute this to his secret 'vice.'
He is explicitly promoted to 'le fidèle des fidèles, une seconde princesse Sherbatoff,' delegated Mme Verdurin's own hosting duties.
He moves from an uncertain outsider left to his own compartment to someone actively sought out, absorbed into the clan's intimacy, and even housed overnight at the Raspelière.
He moves from 'ennuyeux' (undesirable) to 'exquis' (prized) in the Verdurins' reckoning.
He crosses into the Verdurins' inner circle at the Raspelière, visiting 'en garçon,' a threshold ordinary Parisian social calculation would not have let him cross.
Mme Verdurin's private jab casts doubt on his intelligence even as she uses him to enhance her own gathering's prestige.

ambiguities: Cottard privately pities Charlus as friendless and self-humiliating ('il n'a pas de relations, il s'humilie'), a judgment the passage itself undercuts by later noting Charlus's claimed kinship to the duc de Guermantes; this layered irony colors E1 but was not scored as a separate event since it is subordinate color within the same overall elevation movement.
